messages:
support: customer `acme-inc` opened a ticket — p99 on /v1/generate (us-west-2) jumped to ~3.5s at 08:22 UTC, baseline ~700ms. No 5xxs, just long tail. Ticket #3427 with sample request + timeline: https://redwoodinc.atlassian.net/browse/SD-3427

alex: on it, grabbing metrics and traces now

sre-bot: Alert triggered: route=/v1/generate region=us-west-2 p99=3.5s p95=1.1s qlen spikes observed on continuous-batcher-03. hold_window_ms=15, target_batch_size=16 — see metrics: https://grafana.local/d/continuous/CB-03

maya: can someone check request size distribution? tiny prompts cause weird batching behavior lately

julio: I pulled histograms — 78% of requests in last hour are < 64 tokens. Inter-arrival has microbursts: many 1-2 reqs in 5-10ms, then silence. Continuous batcher waits up to hold_window to fill, so you get either tiny single-item batches or big aggregated batches that blow past KV cache warmups -> long tail when cache misses cascade

alex: repro quick locally: run 1000 clients sending short prompts with poisson bursts, observe p99 > 2s. command I used:
```
# spike repro (local)
for i in {1..1000}; do (
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"input":"hi","max_tokens":32}' &
); sleep 0.005; done
```

ken: thanks. question: is the issue strictly hold_window_ms too long, or is target_batch_size interacting with autoscaling/packing?

julio: both. When hold_window is long, packer tries to assemble >16 reqs which increases GPU kernel runtimes and occasionally triggers bigger-than-expected CUDA memory peaks; autoscaler then shuffles pods and that creates extra latency for inflight requests. Also prefix/KV-cache thrash on long batches for short prompts -> disproportionate p99

maya: short-term mitigation options: 1) lower hold_window_ms on that route (e.g., 4ms) 2) set min_batch_size=1 for the route to effectively bypass batching for tiny prompts 3) enable aggressive prefix caching for this model 4) route that customer to lower-concurrency pool (dedicated) while we investigate

alex: I can flip a canary. Proposed command (internal):
```
rzctl route update --route /v1/generate --region us-west-2 \
  --batcher hold_window_ms=4,min_batch_size=1 --canary 10%
```

support: can we do that ASAP? customer is on paid plan and seeing user regressions

ken: I'll run the canary now on 10% of traffic, monitor p95/p99 and CPU/GPU mem.

sre-bot: Deploy event: route-update started by ken at 08:34 UTC — canary=10% — diff: hold_window_ms 15 -> 4, min_batch_size 1 -> 1

(5m pass)
ken: initial telemetry: canary hosts show p99 down to ~850ms, p95 ~420ms. Overall cluster p99 still at 2.9s because majority traffic still on old config

julio: good signal. plan: ramp to 50% in 10m if metrics hold, otherwise rollback. Also open follow-up to evaluate smarter dynamic hold window (adaptive per inter-arrival)

alex: created postmortem/ticket: SD-3430 "continuous-batcher hold_window mis-tune caused p99 spike for short prompts" — adding owner: julia (eng-runtime), ETA: patch + adaptive experiment by EOD

maya: action items:
- temp: ramp canary to 50% if canary p99 < 1s for 15m
- medium: enable prefix caching and run load tests
- long: implement inter-arrival-aware adaptive hold window and add route-level min_batch_size heuristics

support: I've updated customer with status: temporary workaround deployed as canary, monitoring. They asked for ETA; gave rough timeline.

alex: tagging in #product to note that short-prompt PLG flows can cause these spikes — we should consider default min_batch_size for low-token routes

ken: will follow the ramp and post metrics. :thumbsup:

julio: leaving notes in the config repo about the change and the reasoning.

sre-bot: Alert resolved for canary hosts. Global alert still present; monitoring ongoing.

support: thanks all — keeping ticket open until global p99 back to baseline and adaptive change in backlog
